items.detail: Types, declarations, statements and expressions as tagged nodes; the JSON Schema is generated from the model and drift-checked.
items.label: cir/1, defined once in Rust

items.detail: An unknown field, an unknown kind, an expression without a type and any format other than cir/1 are refused.
items.label: Strict reading

items.detail: One byte sequence per document; codespec validate --canonical refuses any other.
items.label: Canonical encoding

items.detail: codespec-read-go lifts one Go package; reading twice gives the same bytes, equal to the checked-in document of every example.
items.label: Go reader on go/types

items.detail: A construct cir/1 cannot express (a goroutine) is kept verbatim as a foreign statement and listed as a refusal; the Rust writer then refuses the function holding it.
items.label: Foreign statements and refusals

items.detail: codespec-read-rust lifts a crate's src/lib.rs into cir/1 with syn and its own name and type resolution for the cir/1 subset; the Rust writer's orders output reads back to the passed document but for four named exceptions, one its loop over a BTreeMap of string keys, which it refuses.
items.label: Rust reader on syn

items.detail: A trait object, a generic function, a closure, unsafe or an integer literal nothing types is kept as a foreign Rust statement with a refusal at its line.
items.label: Rust outside the subset is kept, not guessed

items.detail: A comma-ok map lookup followed by an early-return guard becomes one lookup_else statement.
items.label: lookup-guard

items.detail: shared, messages, fallible, comma_ok, read_only, displays and unordered_iteration, computed once per module for every writer.
items.label: Seven facts

items.detail: codespec pass over its own output gives the same bytes.
items.label: Passes reach their fixed point in one run

items.detail: codespec-write-go writes gofmt-clean, vetted Go; the reader reads it back to the same cir/1.
items.label: Go writer on go/ast and go/printer

items.detail: codespec-write-rust writes a Cargo crate from the module and its facts; the crate builds without warnings.
items.label: Rust writer on syn and prettyplease

items.detail: A module without facts is refused whole by the Rust writer, naming the pass to run.
items.label: Writers decide nothing the facts do not say

items.detail: The original Go, the Go output and the Rust output of orders agree on 200 traces of 300 commands.
items.label: Byte-for-byte comparison on seeded traces

items.detail: A one-token change in the Rust output exits 1 naming the seed, the implementation and the first differing line.
items.label: A planted change is caught

items.detail: SplitMix64 and integer arithmetic only: one seed gives the same trace bytes everywhere.
items.label: Traces pinned across platforms

items.detail: A Go order service read, passed, written as Go and as Rust, and compared under the harness.
items.label: orders

items.detail: A Go greeting service written as Go and as Rust with no refusal; the showcase page is generated from its files.
items.label: greeter

items.detail: A hand-written Rust crate read, passed and written as Go and as Rust; the original, the Go output and the Rust output agree on 200 traces of 300 commands.
items.label: inventory

items.detail: An algorithmic Go package: for loops with break and continue, switch, slices and integer arithmetic that wraps on overflow. Read, passed, written as Go and as Rust with no refusal; the original, the Go output and the Rust output agree on 200 traces of 300 commands.
items.label: series

items.detail: validate, schema, features, read, pass, write, conform and harness.
items.label: codespec command line

items.detail: codespec conform runs codespec-read-go over its corpus, one Go source per claimed feature: each runs to the case's expected output, reads twice to the same bytes, uses its feature outside a foreign statement, and written as Go runs to the expected output again.
items.label: Go reader conforms to the kit

items.detail: codespec conform runs codespec-read-rust over its corpus, one Rust crate per claimed feature, through the same four steps as the Go reader.
items.label: Rust reader conforms to the kit

items.detail: codespec conform runs codespec-read-java over its corpus, one Java source per claimed feature, through the same four steps as the Go reader; codespec-run-java runs each source to the case's expected output first.
items.label: Java reader conforms to the kit

items.detail: codespec conform runs codespec-read-groovy over its corpus, the kit's Java sources compiled as Groovy 2.4, through the same four steps as the Go reader; codespec-run-groovy runs each source to the case's expected output first.
items.label: Groovy reader conforms to the kit

items.detail: codespec conform runs codespec-read-c over its corpus, one C source per claimed feature, through the same four steps as the Go reader; codespec-run-c runs each source to the case's expected output first.
items.label: C reader conforms to the kit

items.detail: codespec conform writes every case of the kit with codespec-write-go, twice to the same bytes, and runs it with codespec-run-go: every claimed feature gives the expected output, every unclaimed one is refused or right, and the boundary cases pass.
items.label: Go writer conforms to the kit

items.detail: codespec conform writes every case of the kit with codespec-write-rust and runs it with codespec-run-rust, as for the Go writer; a module without facts is refused naming codespec pass.
items.label: Rust writer conforms to the kit

items.detail: codespec conform --lang cir --role writer copies every case of the kit with codespec-write-cir and runs it with the evaluator through codespec-run-cir; it claims every feature but the two it gives a reason for, stmt.foreign, which it refuses, and intrinsic.append, whose case passes.
items.label: Evaluator writer conforms to the kit

items.detail: Every exported function of the series and inventory examples gets 200 seeded calls, a method through a generated probe that builds its receiver, and the evaluator, codespec-run-go and codespec-run-rust print the same bytes; Inventory.Find is not run as Rust, whose writer refuses every call of a comma-ok function.
items.label: Differential runs against the evaluator

items.detail: codespec conform writes every case of the kit with codespec-write-c and runs it with codespec-run-c, which compiles the C11 with cc, as for the Go writer.
items.label: C writer conforms to the kit

items.detail: A call of a function of another package is an extern call, declared with its signature; the Go reader reads standard library calls so and the Go writer writes them back, the Rust writer refuses them.
items.label: Extern calls

items.detail: codespec effects reports per function the effects it may have (db, env, fs.read, fs.write, io, net, proc, rand, stdin, stdout, time) from summaries of the functions outside the module, and lists every call or statement it cannot account for as unknown.
items.label: Effects report

items.detail: codespec eval runs a cir/1 module on a calls file with a tree-walking interpreter and prints what the kit's native runners print; every kit case gives its expected output twice byte-equal, and a run that executes a foreign statement or calls an extern without a built-in handler stops naming the node.
items.label: Evaluator

source: codespec-docs, from its capability list; every shipped item names the test or gate task that holds it
